prompt: Show gradient descent from w = 3 on L(w) = w²/2. Let me choose learning rates 0.2, 0.8, 1.2 and 2.1 and inspect steps 0 through 8. Show convergence, shrinking overshoots and divergence with all points visible.
path: The dev clone's composer with the learner's own words (no slash command): the chat router classified the line, then the brief's Generate. No fixture was seeded or copied; the author, review and repair ran on the real backend.

brief:
Review explanation

Gradient descent on L(w) = w²/2 with four learning rates

interactive
Show gradient descent from w = 3 on L(w) = w²/2. Let me choose learning rates 0.2, 0.8, 1.2 and 2.1 and inspect steps 0 through 8. Show convergence, shrinking overshoots and divergence with all points visible.

Presentation
Static
Steps
Over time
Experiment

You'll see the bowl-shaped curve L(w) = w²/2 with gradient descent points starting at w = 3. Arrows connect each point to the next, and the update rule w ← (1 − η)·w is shown with the current w and loss values. When you choose a step from 0 to 8, the path grows one point at a time. The axes are sized so every point stays visible, even the far-out ones for the largest rate. Choosing a learning rate of 0.2, 0.8, 1.2 or 2.1 lets you see that each step multiplies w by 1 − η. That gives slow steady convergence, fast convergence, overshoots that switch sides and shrink, or overshoots that grow until the path diverges.

ASSUMPTIONS 1
LIMITATIONS 3

manifest.title: Gradient descent on L(w) = w²/2 with four learning rates
manifest.summary: Gradient descent starts at w = 3 on the bowl L(w) = w²/2. Because the gradient is w, each step is w ← w − ηw = (1 − η)·w. Pick a learning rate and move the step from 0 to 8 to grow the path one point at a time: 0.2 converges slowly, 0.8 converges fast without crossing, 1.2 crosses sides with shrinking overshoots, 2.1 crosses sides with growing overshoots and diverges.
assumptions: Plain gradient descent with a fixed learning rate and exact gradient L'(w) = w; no momentum or noise.
Only steps 0 to 8 are shown. Axes span w from −3.5 to 3.5 for rates 0.2, 0.8 and 1.2, and widen to −7 to 7 for rate 2.1 so its path (|w| ≈ 6.4 at step 8) stays visible.
Iterates that converge very close to 0 (rate 0.8) can still overlap at the minimum.
One learning rate is drawn at a time.
manifest.description: A parabola L(w) = w²/2 is drawn over w from −3.5 to 3.5 (or −7 to 7 for rate 2.1), with a loss scale on the left. Dots mark gradient descent iterates starting at w = 3, joined by arrows from each point to the next; the latest point is larger. A panel on the right shows the update rule w_{k+1} = w_k − ηw_k = (1 − η)w_k over two lines, the chosen η and factor 1 − η, the step k, the current w and loss, and whether the path converges or diverges based on whether |1 − η| is below 1.

brief.title: Gradient descent on L(w) = w²/2 with four learning rates
brief.summary: You'll see the bowl-shaped curve L(w) = w²/2 with gradient descent points starting at w = 3. Arrows connect each point to the next, and the update rule w ← (1 − η)·w is shown with the current w and loss values. When you choose a step from 0 to 8, the path grows one point at a time. The axes are sized so every point stays visible, even the far-out ones for the largest rate. Choosing a learning rate of 0.2, 0.8, 1.2 or 2.1 lets you see that each step multiplies w by 1 − η. That gives slow steady convergence, fast convergence, overshoots that switch sides and shrink, or overshoots that grow until the path diverges.
assumptions: Plain gradient descent with a fixed learning rate and exact gradient L'(w) = w, with no momentum or noise.
limitations: With rate 0.8 the factor is 0.2, so it converges quickly without overshooting. The shrinking overshoots come from rate 1.2.
Only steps 0 to 8 are shown. With rate 2.1, w reaches about 6.4 by step 8, so the axes are wide and early steps for small rates look tightly bunched.
Only one rate is drawn at a time, not all four side by side.
